Importantly, “exertional *and* nighttime” shortness of breath in a smoker — even without orthopnea — may reflect nocturnal bronchoconstriction or early ventilatory limitation, not heart failure (BNP pending, no orthopnea/PND). So the most parsimonious, evidence-grounded, and guideline-aligned diagnosis *at this stage* — pending spirometry — is **COPD**, as the leading cause of new-onset obstructive symptoms in this demographic.
